clue.text: Caught bird, chicken

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a raven is a large black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bird has been trapped, and it happens to be a chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' looks like the bird that was caught, but here it is the adjective meaning cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal or literary synonyms for cowardly, lacking any courage.

clue.text: Said bridle on top must be restored

indicators.note: in a down entry the bridle word sits above the other piece

parts.note: a rein is part of a horse's bridle, used by metonymy for it
said means stated

explanation.surface: A spoken order that the horse's bridle must be put back on top.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top' means the first piece comes higher in the grid, so it goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something restored has been put back into its former place or position.

clue.text: Siren volume is linked with power unit

parts.note: an amp (ampere) is a unit of electric current, loosely a power unit

explanation.surface: A siren's loudness depends on the amplifier it is wired to.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman who lures men, a femme fatale, is called both.

clue.text: Salerno possibly somewhere in the USA?

parts.note: the town name Salerno is one possible new arrangement of the letters of Orleans, with 'new' as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: Asks whether the Italian port of Salerno might have a namesake somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, with 'new' signalling an anagram of ORLEANS, and that anagram is SALERNO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louisiana jazz city on the Mississippi is a place in the United States.

clue.text: Disowned sailor Jack, awfully rude

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor
J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word rude is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack, having been terribly rude, is cast off by his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' looks like it qualifies the rudeness, but it signals the anagram making URED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to abjure something is to renounce or formally reject it, as one disowns a belief.

clue.text: Loud variety turn in reality

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a turn on a variety bill is an act

explanation.surface: A noisy music-hall performance takes place in real life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word: the answer means reality, as in the phrase 'in fact'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is true and actually exists, rather than imagined, is a matter of truth.

clue.text: Can man's following study delegation?

indicators.note: the can and man pieces follow the study piece in the answer

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a tin is a can
a gent is a man; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fellow's follow-on study could be done by a delegation.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of representatives sent to a meeting is a party or delegation.

clue.text: Being least active, I had to take the continental way

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd
le is French for the
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: Feeling sluggish, someone chose the lazy European route.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of idle describes whoever does the least work or is most inactive.

clue.text: Decorated doctor ambled round area

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the area word
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of ambled are altered

parts.note: a zone is an area

explanation.surface: A medical practitioner ambled round a part of town, sporting medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is the verb, not the physician: tampering produces EMBLAD, which goes 'round' the area word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a shield or banner decorated with a coat of arms or bright design is described this way.

clue.text: Expert boards last tube — result, finally

indicators.note: boarding a vehicle means getting into it, so the expert goes inside

parts.note: end means last, the final part
a duct is a tube or channel
a pro, professional, is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist gets on the final Underground train, and gets a result at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' suggests the London Underground but means a pipe; 'boards' means gets on, so the expert goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The final outcome of a process is what one gets ultimately, its eventual result.

clue.text: Spell 'Discharge' backwards

indicators.note: backwards tells the solver to read the discharge word from right to left

parts.note: to emit is to discharge

explanation.surface: An instruction to write a word out in reverse order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like an instruction to write letters, but it is the noun for a period.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period or stretch, as in a spell abroad.

clue.text: 11 kept in by teacher after sentence one's put here

indicators.note: being kept in means being held inside, so the teacher word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
the answer to 11 Across is a period, abbreviated T as in physics

explanation.surface: A pupil is kept in detention by a teacher after being given a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 Across is TIME, here shortened to its abbreviation T. 'Kept in' looks like school detention, which suits the prison definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for prison, where a convicted person is sent to serve a term.

clue.text: Going up the wall? Take this

definitions.text: Going up the wall? Take this

parts.words: Going up the wall? Take this
parts.note: going up the wall usually means getting angry, but here it is literal: a climbing aid made of cords with rungs

explanation.surface: Advice for someone getting exasperated: take something to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: A flexible climbing aid with cords and rungs lets you scale a wall.

clue.text: Officer in place — occupier

parts.note: lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'
a tenant occupies a property

explanation.surface: An official in post, holding the position someone occupies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in place' hints at the phrase 'in lieu', which supplies LIEU.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior commissioned rank in the army or navy is an officer.

clue.text: Performing Lear, hit act gets histrionic

indicators.note: performing suggests the words are put through their paces in a new order

explanation.surface: An actor playing King Lear in a hit show becomes over-dramatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe exaggerated, stagey behaviour meant for effect.

clue.text: What smells delightful, almost grand, in rapid decline?

parts.note: the nose is what one smells with

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the delightful word is dropped

parts.note: divine means delightful
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Asks what sweet scent could accompany a steep fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging steeply, like an aircraft heading for the ground, describes a rapid decline.

clue.text: The old man with good vessel's capsized — substitute required

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in an across clue the whole string is turned round

parts.note: one's old man is one's father, pa
pots are vessels, read as plural

explanation.surface: Father's fine boat has overturned, so a replacement is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary measure filling a gap until something better comes along is a makeshift substitute.

clue.text: Verbal hesitation in retreat, poetry's back

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the hesitation word is turned around

parts.note: er is the sound of verbal hesitation
verse is poetry; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A stammering retreat, with poetry making a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a car is to drive it in the rearward direction.

clue.text: London area team touring a place on the coast

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the team pieces go around the a

parts.note: SE is a London postcode district, south-east
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A London team on tour visits a resort beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is a London postal district (south-east).
explanation.definitionFit: A coastal resort area by the sea, such as a beach town, is this.

clue.text: Len coasted aimlessly in youth

indicators.note: moving aimlessly means without direction, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Len drifted aimlessly through his teenage years.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager, a young person between childhood and adulthood, is a youth.

clue.text: Advanced celebrity houses left burning

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: to house something is to contain it, so the left letter goes inside

parts.note: fame is celebrity

explanation.surface: A well-known star's homes left on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something on fire, ablaze with flames, is burning.

clue.text: Orderly found in dirty ditch after falling over

indicators.note: falling over turns the extracted letters round so they read right to left
found in signals the letters are inside the words dirty ditch

explanation.surface: A neat hospital attendant discovered in a filthy trench after a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' extracts YDIT from dirTY DITch, and 'after falling over' reverses it. 'Orderly' looks like the hospital attendant, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: neat and well arranged, everything in its place.

clue.text: Lake as well as countryside

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake on maps
and means as well as

explanation.surface: Lakes and rural scenery together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground, open territory or rural terrain is countryside.

clue.text: Diana's letter is contemptuous

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, so Diana's is Di's
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A letter from Diana is scornful in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: treating something as unworthy of consideration, with scorn.

clue.text: Protest as one of us served up in party

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the party word

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: in a down entry served up means sent upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: me is one of the people meant by us

explanation.surface: A complaint from one guest about how food was served at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns the pronoun round to EM; 'served' tempts a food reading but only signals direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for demonstration, a public march or protest.

clue.text: Some risk increasing personal cover

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Reads like insurance jargon: some risk is rising, so personal cover is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of the body is literally the covering each person wears.

clue.text: Maxim I reproduced involving two editors using various arts

indicators.note: reproduced suggests the letters are produced again in a new order

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, so two editors give ED twice

explanation.surface: A saying is copied out by two newspaper editors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' brings the two EDs into the pool with MAXIM I before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Artwork combining several materials or media, such as paint and collage, uses various arts.

clue.text: Payment for written material coming from Ealing

indicators.note: coming from suggests the letters are made out of the place name by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A journalist's fee for an article sent from Ealing, a west London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: Payment to a writer calculated per printed line of text.
